comments.author: Jordan Jones
comments.text:
Diagnosis on Preheim voltage drop issue:

Box 2 (590 D4) pulled.
Tested our cheap miliohmeter on the MEB_S3 and misc. busbars.
The tool: I'm not 100% convinced on the absolute values, which seem higher than should be expected even in a 'perfect' scenario... I think we can chalk that up to the quality of the leads. This Amazon special is like $130 total... Hioki leads by themselves are $250-$750.The tool itself is solid. Consistent, reliable readings, maintains it's 'zero' point, you can re-test the same connection after testing a few others and the value is accurate to the uOhm. So these values are useful compared to themselves, not to what we actually expect if we were measuring with a $2000 meter.

What I found is that there was a lack of contact at all three of the 'lateral' busbars (going from side-to-side on a module).

You can see this in the NOOXID pattern on the busbars. The module connections which had the worst values had the smallest area of NOOXID compression.

This is primarily due to insufficient material cut out of the protective housing on the 590s.  This caused the plastic to be .5mm-1.5mm proud of the terminal, causing the busbar to not make full contact. You could also see a small amount of plastic being smashed between the busbar and the terminal.

A secondary cause was excessive insulation on the busbars, which interfered with the plastic housing.

It wasn't pretty, but I was able to trim down the excess plastic using fine snips to where no further material was proud. I also trimmed back the insulation where necessary. This would be much more easily accomplished prior to installation.

Measurements were taken from internal-module-busbar directly adjacent to the desired joint to be measured. Meter was zerod to this value to reduce discrepancies relating to mating surface.

comments.author: Jordan Jones
comments.text:
Troubleshoot voltage issue — work performed August 10, 2026
I set up the Vici VC480C+ micro-ohmmeter on the 20 mΩ range and verified its zero behavior by re-zeroing on a terminal-to-terminal placement and re-measuring each joint. Implied offset was 0.69 / 0.73 / 0.68 mΩ across spans of 1.19–1.92 mΩ, with no relationship to reading magnitude. Repeatability is ±0.025 mΩ. All readings below are terminal-zeroed.
I measured all three module-to-module busbar joints in Box 2 over two passes. As found: 1-to-2 at 1.23 mΩ, 2-to-3 at 0.46 mΩ, 3-to-4 at 0.72 mΩ. Ranking held across both passes.
I pulled the 1-to-2 and 3-to-4 busbars. The NO-OX-ID witness pattern showed partial compression on both. The orange terminal housing on the LYTH VDA590 sits up to 1.7 mm proud of the terminal face and was visibly crushed between busbar and terminal.
I trimmed the housing, applied NO-OX-ID and reinstalled each joint. On 3-to-4 I also found HV insulation fouling the joint face and removed it. 2-to-3 needed the housing cut down but no insulation trim.
Results

undefined
3-to-4 read 0.56 mΩ reinstalled dry, before insulation removal and NO-OX-ID.
Documented with 72 photos.

comments.author: Jordan Jones
comments.text:
TLDR: Anyone building 590s be very sure that these plastic housings are cut well below the face of the terminal.

We will need to pull the other two boxes to rectify. The other D4 will be a similar procedure to this box. The D8 will need to be disassembled to the point we can access the inner busbars.

comments.author: Jordan Jones
comments.text:
Issues:
Very small brake fluid leak from the brake switch sensor. Brake sensor is functional but you have to get very deep into the pedal for it to engage. Might warrant replacement (did not come with new booster). There was no seal on the original I took off, but perhaps there should be one. Will get one.
Vacuum is bleeding out of the booster, causing the pump to cycle on approximately every 45 seconds.  If the vacuum line is plugged before the booster it holds vacuum perfectly. With the booster installed there is a slow leak. I tightened all the hardware and the leak decreased significantly but is still present. Reaching out to the rebuilder for his advice.
GUI speedo is about 50% slow.
Peterson instrumentation not showing any values.
Speaker interference noise, both from power steering input and throttle application.
Steering wheel is not centered.
Front left drum seems like it may be sticking.
Estop non-functional (see above)
Heater not functional (will come online with PMUs)
PRD dimming/lighting non-functional.
Powertrain coolant loop is cavitating. I think it needs another vacuum bleed after the coolant leak.

comments.author: Jordan Jones
comments.text:
Re-installed interior, with 'external' PRD buttons so we can troubleshoot the PRD dimming issue.
Put vehicle back on ground.
Installed a port for vacuum-testing the brake booster system.
23 in/hg achieved. When vacuum drops to 18in/hg the pump kicks back on.
Cycling every 15 seconds.
With the booster removed from the system, and the line going to the booster plugged, no leakage was detected. 23in/hg steady.
With the booster installed, leakage continues.
Tightened all external hardware. Leakage reduced. Cycling every 40 seconds now.
Test-drove for the first time. Noticed scraping from rear of vehicle.
After diagnosis, discovered the new pins that came with the brake kit had holes that were 3mm too long, allowing the shoe  to contact the drum. Found the original pins and reinstalled. Issue resolved.
E-stop was disabled by @Devin DuMont during the brake diagnosis, however during that process it appears the e-stop was toasted, possibly by receiving a constant run signal. E-stop no longer functional. Checked vehicle-side, voltages as expected. Attempted to apply voltage to e-stop side: no movement. New e-stop required.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Test drove with laptop looking for CAN1 errors. Catching about 870 per second all in one large group. Turned off OBDII from the inverter which didn't help. Also tried turning off diag data. Turned them back on and unplugged the logger which is set to auto-baud. Still no change. Used Kvaser set at 1000mbps and I get a message to decode with data 2044, 2046, and 2048. Test driving is getting difficult since CAN errors occasionally cause the VCU to drop PreCharge.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Removed all CAN messages from both PMU's re-tested for CAN errors, still there. Removed CAN1 wiring to PMU's and re-tested. No luck.

comments.text: Tested out external CAN connection to the inverter. Problem went away momentarily. Tested alternate VCU. Problem still exists. Decided to buy PicoScope to help analyze.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Reviewed PEAK codebase for good starting point. Setup project for basic router. Modified, commented, & compiled.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Worked with Jordan and Dusty to use the PicoScope on CAN1 crashing issue. Hooked up to CAN1 at various spots. Tried grounding shields. Verified waveforms against Buck.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Re-checked vehicle faults after Jordan replaced the ground to the inverter. Noise problem stopped with a larger ground but also didn't come back with the old #22 wire back installed. Was able to drive the vehicle shortly till the problem resurfaced causing the positive contactor to weld. Verified this with Ampere and used the BMS test box to break the weld since the vehicle logic does not allow. Checked the whole vehicle again and the noise problem still exists. Tried unplugging all HV accessories, no luck. Installed a minimal external CAN1 network with all new wiring and found the CAN1L wire pulled out of the terminal at the inverter while removing that wire. Tested with new CAN network and PicoScope looks noisy like before. Tried grounding shield, still no luck.

comments.author: Devin DuMont
comments.text: Re-verified noise exists on external CAN harness. Setup provisions to pull in the positive contactor with the BMS disconnected. Had a remote session with Andrew to force the VCU into enabling the inverter with the BMS missing. Noise still present on external CAN1 network. Repeated various trials. Discovered HVIL in the JB wasn't working correctly, replaced. Noise still present. Decided to isolate inverter as much as possible from vehicle. Modified Python gauges test script to enable inverter for 500ms. Setup completely isolated inverter harness & provisions to pre-charge. Tested both VCU CAN and INV CAN but both still had noise. Added motor case and inverter case into the PicoScope, and re-tested. Found ~10V between chassis ground and motor case. Installed #4 AWG wire between motor case, inverter case and battery negative stud. Re-tested and still found noise. Moved #4 AWG to ground distribution blocks, re-tested, and still have noise.
